answer: Identity-seeded verifiable delay resists sybils: minting each identity requires evaluating a VDF — a strictly sequential computation seeded from that identity's own key — that no amount of parallel cores can speed up for a single eval. One velvet-smooth machine must run each head's delay in full: k fakes cost k sequential evaluations, so serially the wait is k times T, and buying parallel hardware to pulse them all at once costs k devices. No relic of batching shortcuts it, since each VDF is identity-bound and cannot be shared. Precondition: the VDF is sequential and per-identity seeded.
